title: Retirement playbook for legacy multiplexed transport and offline-replay adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The legacy multiplexed transport (multiplex-v1) and its offline-replay adapter were introduced as an experimental low-latency transport to multiplex multiple logical channels over a single persistent connection and to allow clients to replay missed events from device-local buffers. Over the last 24 months this path has accrued operational complexity, subtle ordering bugs, and an outsized maintenance burden on infra and security teams. The new unified streaming API (sse/v2 + event-archive) and the client-side durable queue in SDKs provide the same guarantees with simpler semantics and stronger observability. Goal: Orchestrate a low-risk, well-communicated retirement of multiplex-v1 and offline-replay adapter, provide first-class migration tooling and a short-lived compatibility shim for laggard clients, and ensure zero unplanned customer-impact for high-value customers.
background: Multiplex-v1 exhibits three recurring incidents: message reordering with larger fanout, head-of-line blocking under network flaps, and subtle auth token scoping gaps. Offline-replay adapter bypassed server-side audit checks in some failure modes. Both features increase the attack surface and block SLO improvements (we cannot safely guarantee ordering SLA). The new architecture centralizes routing, supports deterministic per-channel ordering, and archives events for server-side replay that integrates with KMS-backed audit logs.
out_of_scope: Removing multiplexed protocol support from third-party OSS SDKs (we will offer adapters but not auto-remove OSS docs in this project). Rewriting customer application logic; we will provide migration guides and tools but not execute migrations for customers except for enterprise support engagements.
goals: Provide a documented, tested migration path that covers 99% of active customers within 90 days of announcement
Ship an open-source compat adapter (client-side) and a server-side short-lived shim to reduce immediate breakage
Ensure observability and regressions detection: define metrics and alerting for migration progress and critical failures
Remove multiplex-v1 and offline-replay adapter from hosted runtime after a 180-day transition window, unless blocked by enterprise exceptions
acceptance_criteria: Migration docs published with step-by-step examples for JS, Python, and Go SDKs
Compat adapter released (npm/pypi/github) and used by at least 50% of remaining clients within first 30 days
Customer impact SAG (support action group) created and staffed for 120 days with runbook
Telemetry: synthesis shows <0.1% error-rate attributable to transport incompatibility after canary rollout
SLA and audit tests updated (ordering, replay, auth) and included in CI for runtime-1.28
Executive sign-off from PM, Eng Director, and Security on final shutdown date
migration_steps: Technical announcement + timeline (D+0): publish deprecation notice, FAQ, and migration guide in docs and email active API keys
SDK updates (D+7): land SDK changes that default to unified streaming and expose compatibility shim opt-in
Compat adapter release (D+14): publish OSS adapter that translates multiplex-v1 semantics to unified streaming for clients that cannot update immediately
Canary runtime shim (D+21): deploy server-side shim in limited region to translate incoming multiplex-v1 traffic to internal routing with enhanced logging
Telemetry gating (D+28): enable migration dashboards and alerts; begin weekly migration review with support/engineering
Customer outreach (D+30 - D+60): targeted emails/SE outreach for top 50 customers still on multiplex-v1, offer migration assistance
Gradual throttling (D+90): begin soft throttling for new multiplex-v1 connections and show clear client-side error codes to prompt upgrades
Final shutdown (D+180): retire compat shims and fully remove multiplex-v1 and offline-replay adapter from hosted runtime unless exception approved
timeline: 2026-03-17: Public deprecation announcement and FAQ published
2026-09-06: Target final shutdown date (180 days after announcement)
rollout_strategy: Phased: announce widely, ship tooling early, enable a server-side shim for a bounded period (6 months), then progressively tighten acceptance for multiplex-v1 connections. Prioritize top-tier customers with direct engineering assistance and provide enterprise exception process recorded in Confluence. Maintain a transparent migration dashboard with per-customer adoption status.
communication_plan: Day 0: Public blog + docs + status page entry
Week 1: Email to all active API key owners with migration checklist
Ongoing: Weekly migration status in community Slack and a dedicated migration channel
Targeted: SE outreach to top 50 customers and scheduled migration office hours
Pre-shutdown: 30/14/7/1-day reminder cadence to remaining clients
support_plan: Create SAG (support action group) with on-call rota for migration-related incidents. Prepare canned responses, triage checklist, and hotfix playbook. Offer paid migration assistance for enterprise customers with complex integrations. Track escalations in a shared migration board.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Enterprise customers cannot upgrade due to compliance constraints. Mitigation: offer timeboxed enterprise exception and dedicated migration engineering support

Risk: Compat adapter fails to cover an edge-case ordering semantics. Mitigation: instrument edge-case telemetry, maintain server-side shim for an additional buffer period, and prioritize fixes in runtime sprint
Risk: Increased support load during soft-throttling. Mitigation: scale SAG staffing and provide customer self-service diagnostics and SDK log levels
rollback_plan: If critical regressions are detected post-disable, re-enable compat shim and rollback throttling within a 48-hour window. Maintain a snapshot of the previous runtime capable of handling multiplex-v1 traffic for emergency fallback for up to 7 days. Postmortem required within 72 hours of rollback initiation.
notes: This plan intentionally favors a compatibility-first approach to minimize outage risk. Engineering should allocate two 1-week intensive sprints immediately after announcement to address the most common adapter edge cases. Legal has flagged audit gaps for offline-replay; Security is already scoped for a small hardening sprint (ENG-29801).
